issues.issue: Did the RPD unreasonably decide the cessation under paragraph 108(1)(a) rather than 108(1)(e)?
issues.applicant_position: Cessation should rest only on 108(1)(e), the change in circumstances when she gave up Falun Gong; the RPD had to fix one cessation date.
issues.respondent_position: The RPD may consider any ground in s. 108(1) and weigh the whole sequence of events; no single cessation date is required.
issues.result_quote: I find that the RPD’s exercise of its discretion to determine the Minister’s application pursuant to paragraph 108(1)(a) was reasonable and intelligibly explained.

issues.issue: Did the RPD unreasonably find that she voluntarily reavailed herself of China's protection?
issues.applicant_position: Her trips were not voluntary, and giving up Falun Gong for the passport was persecution, not receipt of protection from China.
issues.respondent_position: Two passports and repeated open trips to China raise a presumption of reavailment that she did not rebut.
issues.result_quote: I find that the RPD reasonably concluded that the Applicant failed to rebut the presumption that she intended to reavail herself of the protection of China.
